subject: general
question: Which of the following tissues makes the plant hard and stiff?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sclerenchyma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sclerenchyma** is a type of plant tissue that provides **mechanical support** to the plant and makes it **hard and stiff**. It is the main strengthening tissue in plants.
 
• The cells of sclerenchyma are characterized by their **thickened, lignified cell walls**, which provide rigidity and durability.
 
• Sclerenchyma cells are typically **dead at maturity**. They lack protoplasm, making them well-suited to their role as a support structure.
 
• There are two types of sclerenchyma cells: **fibers** (elongated cells) and **sclereids** (short, irregularly shaped cells). Both contribute to the hardness of plant parts, such as seed coats, nutshells, and vascular bundles.
 
• Common examples of sclerenchyma include **coconut husk fibers** and the gritty texture in guava or pear, which is due to sclereids.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Collenchyma:**

 
 
• Collenchyma cells have **unevenly thickened cell walls**, primarily composed of cellulose and pectin.
 
• This tissue provides **flexibility and mechanical support** to growing parts of the plant, such as stems and leaves.
 
• Unlike sclerenchyma, collenchyma cells are **living at maturity** and have a protoplasm.
 
 
 
• **Aerenchyma:**
 
 
• Aerenchyma is a specialized parenchyma tissue with large air spaces that facilitate **gas exchange** and buoyancy in aquatic plants.
 
• It is commonly found in plants like **water hyacinth** and **lotus**, where it helps the plant to float.
 
 
 
• **Chlorenchyma:**
 
 
• Chlorenchyma cells contain abundant **chloroplasts** and are involved in **photosynthesis**.
 
• This tissue is present in the mesophyll of leaves and other green parts of plants.
 
• Chlorenchyma contributes to the production of food in plants through the process of photosynthesis.
 
 
 
• **Sclerenchyma Characteristics:**
 
 
• **Location:** Found in stems, roots, vascular bundles, and hard parts like seed coats and nutshells.
 
• **Function:** Provides rigidity, durability, and mechanical strength to the plant.
 
• **Examples:** Coconut husk fibers, sclereids in pears, and the hard shell of nuts.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Differences Between Sclerenchyma and Collenchyma:**

 
 
• Sclerenchyma cells are **dead** at maturity, while collenchyma cells are **living**.
 
• Sclerenchyma has **thick lignified walls**, whereas collenchyma walls are **unevenly thickened** and non-lignified.
 
• Collenchyma provides **flexibility**, while sclerenchyma provides **rigidity**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Sclerenchyma:**
 
 
• Used in **rope-making** due to the fibers' strength (e.g., jute and hemp).
 
• Provides structural support in **wood and bamboo** industries.
